node.label: Many-to-one symbols in picture graphs

node.description: Read bar graphs using category labels, bar heights and scale values.

node.label: Make bar graphs
node.description: Create bar graphs from frequency data with suitable labels, scale and spacing.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Axes titles and labels
node.description: Use titles, axes, category labels and units to make data displays interpretable.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose graph scale
node.description: Choose and interpret appropriate scales for bar graphs and other displays.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare categories in graphs
node.description: Compare category frequencies and answer questions using picture and bar graphs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Shape of distribution introduction
node.description: Describe the overall shape of a distribution using visual features of a display.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stem and leaf plots

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Construct histograms

node.label: Box plot features
node.description: Identify median, quartiles, whiskers and range in a box plot.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Construct box plots
node.description: Construct box plots from five-number summaries.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare data displays
node.description: Compare different displays of the same or related data for clarity and appropriateness.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Graphs need labels
node.description: Data displays need clear titles, labels and units so values can be interpreted.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale controls graph reading
node.description: The graph scale determines how counts or values are read from a display.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Picture graph key matters
node.description: A picture graph key tells how many data values each symbol represents.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar height shows frequency
node.description: In a bar graph, bar height or length represents the frequency for a category.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Each dot represents a data value
node.description: In a dot plot, each dot represents one occurrence of a data value unless a key states otherwise.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Distribution shape is a visual pattern
node.description: Clusters, gaps, peaks and spread help describe the visual shape of a distribution.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Histograms group intervals
node.description: A histogram groups numerical data into intervals and shows frequency for each interval.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plots use five number summary
node.description: A box plot displays the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile and maximum.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Display choice matches data type
node.description: Different displays suit categorical, discrete numerical or continuous numerical data.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same data can have multiple displays
node.description: The same data can be represented in different displays that emphasise different features.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Picture symbol always means one
node.description: Learner assumes each picture symbol represents one item even when the key says otherwise.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ignore graph scale
node.description: Learner reads bars, axes or intervals as if every mark increases by one regardless of the scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar area instead of height
node.description: Learner compares bar area or width rather than bar height or length when reading frequencies.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Histogram treated as category bar graph
node.description: Learner treats histogram intervals as unrelated categories rather than ordered numerical intervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plot shows all values
node.description: Learner thinks a box plot displays every individual data value rather than a summary of distribution.

edge.rationale: Reading picture graphs is central to early picture and bar graph work.
Making picture graphs directly practises categorical data display.
One-to-one symbols are an early picture graph convention.
Many-to-one symbols extend picture graph interpretation through keys.
Reading bar graphs is core to picture and bar graph work.
Making bar graphs directly practises frequency display construction.
Titles, axes and labels are required display conventions.
Graph scale controls how bar graphs and similar displays are read.
Comparing categories is a major interpretation task for categorical displays.
Reading dot plots is central to line and dot plot work.
Constructing dot plots directly practises numerical data display.
Line plots are commonly used for measurement data on number lines.
Clusters, gaps and outliers are important visual features in dot and line plots.
Distribution shape extends visual interpretation of dot and line plots.
Stem-and-leaf plots are related numerical distribution displays before histograms and box plots.
Grouped intervals are essential to histogram construction and interpretation.
Histogram interpretation is central to grouped numerical displays.
Constructing histograms applies grouped interval and frequency reasoning.
Box plot features are central to box plot interpretation.
Constructing box plots applies five-number summary display conventions.
Comparing displays helps choose and critique representations of data.
Reading picture graphs requires understanding categories being counted.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts symbols without connecting them to category labels.

edge.rationale: Making picture graphs requires counted or tallied category data.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws symbols without matching data frequencies.

edge.rationale: One-to-one symbol interpretation is an early picture graph reading convention.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot tell how many data values are represented by simple symbols.

edge.rationale: Many-to-one keys extend the simpler one-symbol-one-value convention.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores the key and counts symbols as single values.

edge.rationale: Reading bar graphs depends on understanding category frequencies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads bar appearance without connecting bar height to frequency.

edge.rationale: Making bar graphs builds on understanding how bar graphs encode category frequencies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates bars that do not match the data or scale.

edge.rationale: Axes, titles and labels are understood through reading and constructing basic graphs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws graphs without interpretable labels or units.

edge.rationale: Choosing scale depends on understanding axes and labels.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a scale that skips values inconsistently or hides the data pattern.

edge.rationale: Comparing categories requires reading bar heights or picture graph frequencies accurately.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies categories but cannot compare their frequencies.

edge.rationale: Dot plots require placing values on an ordered scale; the exact number-line prerequisite may vary by data range.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats positions on the dot plot as unordered labels.

edge.rationale: Constructing dot plots builds on reading dots as values and frequencies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner stacks dots inconsistently or loses repeated values.

edge.rationale: Line plots for measurement data require recorded numerical measurements.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots measurements without consistent values or units.

edge.rationale: Identifying clusters, gaps and outliers depends on reading dot and line plots accurately.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads individual values but misses visual features of the distribution.

edge.rationale: Describing distribution shape builds from recognising visual features in displays.
edge.failure_signal: Learner lists values but cannot describe the overall data pattern.

edge.rationale: Stem-and-leaf plots are another ordered display of numerical values and frequencies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot split values into stems and leaves or preserve data order.

edge.rationale: Grouped intervals require interpreting data values along an ordered numerical scale.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates overlapping or uneven intervals unintentionally.

edge.rationale: Histograms display frequencies for grouped numerical intervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats histogram bars as separate categories rather than intervals.

edge.rationale: Constructing histograms builds on interpreting grouped intervals and frequencies.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws separated category bars or miscounts interval frequencies.

edge.rationale: Box plot features require understanding median and quartiles as summary values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads a box plot as raw data rather than summary positions.

edge.rationale: Constructing box plots requires identifying the five-number summary positions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places box, median or whiskers at incorrect values.

edge.rationale: Comparing displays requires familiarity with several display types and what each shows.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses displays without considering data type or interpretive purpose.
